# vcp_vmware_server_network_attachment (Resource)

Attaches a VMware Cloud server to a client network — an `isolated` or a `routed` one.

A server always has a public interface of its own (see `vcp_vmware_server`), so this resource adds private connectivity next to it. Use `vcp_vmware_server_public_interface` for an additional public address.

~> Every attribute forces a new resource: the API recreates the interface when the network or the address changes. Detaching an interface from a running server needs an image that supports NIC hot-remove — otherwise power the server off before applying a change that replaces it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Private connectivity between two servers. Each server already has a public
# interface of its own — that one belongs to vcp_vmware_server.
resource "vcp_vmware_network" "private" {
  type        = "isolated"
  location_id = 5
  name        = "app-private"
  address     = "10.100.0.0"
  mask        = 24
  enable_dhcp = false
}

resource "vcp_vmware_server_network_attachment" "app" {
  server_id  = vcp_vmware_server.app.id
  network_id = vcp_vmware_network.private.id

  # A static address needs the network to have DHCP switched off. Leave it out on
  # a DHCP network and the platform assigns one.
  ip = "10.100.0.10"
}

resource "vcp_vmware_server_network_attachment" "db" {
  server_id  = vcp_vmware_server.db.id
  network_id = vcp_vmware_network.private.id
  ip         = "10.100.0.11"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `network_id` (Number) ID of the client network to attach. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `server_id` (Number) ID of the server. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `ip` (String) Static address on the network. Only a network with DHCP switched off accepts one; leave it unset otherwise and the platform assigns the address. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) ID of the network interface.
- `is_primary` (Boolean) Whether this is the server's primary interface. Always `false` here — the primary interface belongs to `vcp_vmware_server`.
- `mac` (String) MAC address of the interface.
- `number` (Number) Position of the interface on the server.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Attachments are imported as "<server_id>:<nic_id>" — the ID of the network
# interface, which is listed in the server's `nics` attribute.
terraform import vcp_vmware_server_network_attachment.app 5678:9012
```
